setting.title: The Regatta Cup
setting.premise: Ruth Calloway invited five guests to Pine Hollow for the weekend before the lake's annual regatta. On Saturday morning the little engraved Regatta Cup she won last summer is gone from her mantel.
setting.background: Pine Hollow is a two-storey log lodge on a lake. Downstairs: the great room with the fireplace and the mantel, where Ruth keeps her photographs and the cup; the kitchen and its pantry; and the front door. Upstairs: the bedrooms; Lena's window looks out over the dock path. Across the yard is the bunkhouse, and the dock path runs down to the dock and Ruth's boathouse, where she keeps her boat, Mabel. Ruth is hosting the weekend before next Saturday's regatta, Friday to Monday. Friday: everyone arrived in the afternoon, then dinner, and at 10 the skippers' toast in the great room, where Ruth raised the Regatta Cup and set it back on the mantel. Saturday morning the mantel was bare. Ruth, Lena, Marisol and Nell have rooms in the lodge; Hal and Theo share the bunkhouse. The cup is a little pewter trophy with every winner since 1971 engraved round the base, Ruth's name among them three times.
setting.missingItem: the Pine Hollow Regatta Cup, Ruth's small engraved sailing trophy

timeline.text: At the skippers' toast Ruth raises the Regatta Cup and sets it back on the mantel. "Cup on the mantel, skipper on the water."
Ruth goes up to bed.
Hal and Theo walk over to the bunkhouse. Nell is already asleep with her earplugs in.
Lena goes up to her room above the dock path.
Marisol sneaks down to the boathouse to study Ruth's new racing sails under their tarp. Her yellow slicker hangs dry on its hook.
Marisol creeps back through the great room. The cup is still on the mantel. Out in the bunkhouse, Theo slips out past a snoring Hal.
Theo starts a batch of choux pastry in the kitchen, practicing for the pastry school his grandmother doesn't know about.
Hal, awake after all, lets himself in the front door. Theo hears it and hides in the pantry.
Hal lifts the Regatta Cup off the mantel. He has secretly entered his own boat in this year's race, and he wants Ruth's luck off the mantel until it's over.
In the boathouse Hal pulls on Marisol's yellow slicker against the rain, ties the cup in a bait bag and lowers it under the end of the dock. His tobacco pouch ends up in the slicker's pocket.
An owl wakes Lena. From her window she sees the yellow slicker on the dock and takes it for Marisol.
Hal hangs up the dripping slicker and is back in his bunk. Theo follows at 1:50.
Ruth comes down to a bare mantel.
Marisol checks her mooring lines against the wind.
In the bunkhouse Hal asks Theo to say Hal never left his bunk on Friday. Theo, terrified his own night in the kitchen will come out, agrees.
Lena, on her way to the dock to look for the owl, hears the two of them murmuring.
Nell drives to her store to check on the cooler.
Ruth bags her new sails in the boathouse for race week.
Theo stress-bakes in the kitchen.
Hal slips down to the boathouse and takes his tobacco pouch back out of Marisol's slicker. He leaves the door ajar.

guests.name: Ruth Calloway
guests.role: Your host, and three-time winner of the Pine Hollow Regatta
guests.voice: Gracious and a little grand. Full sentences, proper punctuation, sailing expressions, the odd ⚓. Warms right up when complimented.

topics.description: where Ruth was on Friday night, the night the cup disappeared, and when she went to bed

variants.text: I turned in at half past ten, as I always do in race week, and slept until half past six.
Bed at ten-thirty, up at six-thirty. I sleep like a boat on a mooring, I'm afraid. Not a sound.

topics.description: where Ruth was on Saturday night

variants.text: Tonight? An early night, I expect. Ask me in the morning.
Asleep by half past ten again. I heard nothing at all, which I suppose is no help.
In my bed, dead to the world. Forgive me.

topics.description: where Ruth was on Sunday night, including her late trip to the boathouse to bag her sails

variants.text: Sunday night hasn't happened yet, detective!
I went down to the boathouse at half past eleven to bag my new sails for race week. Back up by quarter to twelve, then bed.
Sails into their bags at eleven-thirty, back in the lodge by eleven forty-five. A skipper prepares, cup or no cup.

topics.description: the missing Regatta Cup itself: what it looks like, its engraving, and when it was last seen

variants.text: Little pewter cup, every winner since 1971 engraved round the base, my name three times. I raised it at the toast at ten and put it back on the mantel. By half past six it was gone.
It was on the mantel after the ten o'clock toast. At half past six it wasn't. That's all I know for certain.

topics.description: the great room mantel where the cup stood, and how Ruth found it bare on Saturday morning

variants.text: I came down at half past six and there was just a clean little ring in the dust where it stood.
Bare. Six-thirty Saturday morning. Nothing else touched, not even the photographs.

topics.description: the old lake saying about the winner keeping the cup on the mantel for luck

variants.text: "Cup on the mantel, skipper on the water." Old lake nonsense, of course. Though I haven't lost since I started keeping it there. ⚓
Everyone on this lake knows the saying. Half of them believe it. I'm in the other half. Mostly.

topics.description: next Saturday's regatta and who is crewing on Ruth's boat this year

variants.text: Hal's crewed for me twenty years, but he told me his knee's too bad this year, poor dear. So Theo is trimming the jib for me.
Theo's crewing, since Hal says his knee won't take it. I'll miss Hal's grumbling, honestly.

topics.description: Ruth's own sailing record and her three regatta wins

variants.text: Three years running, thank you for asking! Though who's counting. (I am.)
Three wins in a row in old Mabel. Not bad for a woman who learned to sail at forty. ⚓

topics.description: Ruth's boathouse, her boat Mabel, and the new racing sails kept there under a tarp

variants.text: My new sails are down there under a tarp. And someone had moved that tarp by Saturday morning. I tied it myself, I know how I left it.
Saturday morning the tarp over my new sails had been shifted. Not my knots. Someone's been having a look.

topics.description: the reward Ruth is offering for the cup's return

variants.text: One blueberry pie, no questions asked. It's a very good pie.
The pie offer stands! Lattice top and all.

topics.description: Hal Brewster, Ruth's jib trimmer of twenty years, and his pipe

variants.text: Hal has trimmed my jib for twenty years. Cherry pipe tobacco, always. I'd know him blindfolded.
Dear old Hal. Smells like a cherry pie on fire, that pipe of his, but there's no better hand on a sheet.

topics.description: Marisol Vance, Ruth's sailing rival who lost to her by a boat length

variants.text: Marisol has wanted that cup since I beat her by a boat length. She sails over in that yellow slicker of hers and it hangs in my boathouse all weekend.
We've been rivals since before you were born. That yellow slicker of hers hangs in my boathouse every weekend she's here. But steal my cup? She'd rather beat me fair. I think.

topics.description: Theo, Ruth's grandson, home from engineering school

variants.text: My grandson! Engineering at the state university. He's going to build bridges.
Theo's a treasure. He's been making croissants all weekend, can you imagine? Engineers are so precise.

topics.description: Lena, Ruth's old college roommate, the retired doctor who watches owls

variants.text: Lena and I roomed together at college. Now she spends her nights chasing owls round my dock.

topics.description: Nell Haggerty, who runs the lake store and post office

variants.text: Nell runs the store and the post office. A lovely woman. Tell her nothing you don't want the whole lake to know.

topics.description: anything that happened around the lodge late on Saturday night, such as the whispering Lena heard

variants.text: Nothing's happened yet tonight, thank heavens.
Whispering? I'm the wrong one to ask. I didn't hear a thing.

topics.description: anything that happened late on Sunday night, such as the boathouse door left open

variants.text: Let's hope Sunday is a quiet one.
I was down in the boathouse with my sails until quarter to twelve. Whatever went on after that, I slept through it.

topics.description: who Ruth thinks took her cup, and why

variants.text: I won't point fingers at my own crew. But a rival who lost by a boat length has a long winter to brood. ⚓
Whoever it was knows this lodge and knows that mantel. That narrows it to everyone I love.

topics.description: anything Ruth saw or heard during Friday night, the night of the theft: noises, lights, people up and about

variants.text: I heard nothing at all, I'm sorry to say. Race week; I sleep hard.
Not a sound. The rain on the roof, perhaps, and then nothing until morning. ⚓
I beg your pardon. It's MY cup. With MY name on it. Three times.
Detective, I would no more hide that cup than sink my own boat.

dodges: You'd have to ask someone else about that.
I'm afraid that's out of my waters.
greetings: Welcome aboard, detective. Thank you for coming.
dictionary.goodnight: I'm turning in, detective. Fair winds, and ask me tomorrow.

guests.name: Dr. Lena Sorensen
guests.role: Ruth's college roommate, a retired doctor and keen owl-watcher
guests.voice: Warm, precise and a little breathless. Full sentences, "Oh!", (parenthetical asides), bird facts, the occasional 🦉.

topics.description: where Lena was on Friday night, the night the cup disappeared, and when she went up to bed

variants.text: I went up at quarter to twelve. My room looks over the dock path (the best owl window in the lodge!).
Upstairs by eleven forty-five with a book and my binoculars on the sill. Habit.

topics.description: the figure in a yellow slicker with a flashlight that Lena saw on the dock from her window in the middle of Friday night

variants.text: An owl woke me around 1:25 and I looked out. Someone was on the dock in a yellow slicker, with a flashlight. Marisol's is the yellow one... I assumed it was her. (Please don't tell her I said so.)
Twenty-five past one, give or take. A yellow slicker on the dock, flashlight bobbing. That slicker is Marisol's. I couldn't see a face, mind you.

topics.description: where Lena was on Saturday night: out owl-watching on the dock after midnight

variants.text: Tonight I'm going owling on the dock! Wish me luck. 🦉
Out on the dock from half past twelve with my flask, hoping for that barred owl. Heard it. Didn't see it. Typical!
Owling on the dock from twelve-thirty. Cold, damp, owl-less. Bliss.

topics.description: the low voices Lena overheard from inside the bunkhouse as she walked past late on Saturday night

variants.text: Nothing to report yet, the night is young!
As I passed the bunkhouse, about 12:25, I heard Hal and Theo talking. Low, serious voices. Not the way you talk about the weather.
Hal and Theo, in the bunkhouse, around twenty-five past twelve. Murmuring. I didn't catch the words, and I didn't stop to try. (I wanted to.)

topics.description: where Lena was on Sunday night

variants.text: An early night, I think. Even owl people need sleep.
Asleep by eleven and dead to the world until six. The owl won.

topics.description: what Lena found on her early bird walk on Monday morning: the boathouse door standing open

variants.text: Ask me in the morning, I'll be out with the binoculars at six.
At six this morning the boathouse door was standing ajar. Ruth is particular about that door.

topics.description: the missing Regatta Cup and when Lena last saw it

variants.text: Ruth held it up at the ten o'clock toast and put it back on the mantel. Little pewter thing, all those names round the base.
On the mantel after the toast at ten. I remember because Ruth made us all raise a glass to it. Oh, she loves that cup.

topics.description: Hal's supposedly bad knee, which Lena looked at as a doctor

variants.text: Hal's knee? He had me look at it Friday afternoon. Honestly, I found nothing wrong with it. Better than mine!

topics.description: Lena's birdwatching and the barred owl she keeps trying to spot

variants.text: The barred owl! "Who cooks for you, who cooks for you-all." I've heard it every night and not seen it once. 🦉
Owls fly almost silently, you know. Special feathers. I've been here three nights and it's still winning.

topics.description: next Saturday's regatta and Lena's plans for it

variants.text: I'll be on the committee boat with a thermos and binoculars. Mostly for the herons, if I'm honest.

topics.description: Lena's phone and her bird-call app

variants.text: My phone lives in my coat pocket with the bird-call app open. Very useful, very annoying to everyone else.

topics.description: Ruth, Lena's college roommate and the host

variants.text: Ruth and I roomed together at college. She sails the way she drives. Fast and absolutely certain.

topics.description: Hal, Ruth's longtime crew, and his cherry pipe

variants.text: Hal's a dear. I've been at him for years about that cherry pipe tobacco. I can smell it a room away!
Oh, Hal. Cherry tobacco and weather forecasts, that's Hal.

topics.description: Marisol, Ruth's sailing rival

variants.text: Marisol is... competitive. She and Ruth have been circling each other since the nineties.
Sharp as a tack, Marisol. Not a woman to cross on a start line.

topics.description: Theo, Ruth's grandson, and his baking

variants.text: Theo's a sweetheart. His croissants on Saturday were professional. I mean that literally.

topics.description: Nell, who runs the lake store and post office

variants.text: Nell knows everything about everyone on this lake, bless her. Some of it's even true.

topics.description: who Lena thinks took the cup, and why

variants.text: Oh, I hate this. I keep going round and round and landing on Marisol, and then I feel disloyal. (She does want that cup.)
I'm a doctor, not a detective! But people who insist they're fine usually aren't. (Forty years of medicine taught me that.)
Oh! Me? I was in my room watching for owls. I don't even like pewter.
Detective, I've known Ruth for forty-five years. I'd sooner steal her teeth.

dodges: Hmm, you'd do better asking Ruth.

greetings: Good morning! Have you seen the herons?
dictionary.goodnight: Off to bed (and the window). Ask me tomorrow, detective!

i was asleep. someone's been in that boathouse again and it wasn't me.

variants.text: ruth's a fine sailor. she's also lucky. there's a difference.
we've raced each other for thirty years. she invites me every year so i can watch her gloat.

topics.description: Hal, Ruth's longtime crew, and his pipe

variants.text: hal. ruth's crew. smells like a cherry pie on fire. that pipe.
hal trims a decent jib. puffs that cherry pipe and talks about the weather like it owes him money.

topics.description: Theo, Ruth's grandson

variants.text: the grandson. always in the kitchen. odd hobby for an engineer.

topics.description: Lena, the retired doctor who goes owl-watching

variants.text: lena. sweet. nosy. up all night with binoculars pointed at other people's business.

topics.description: Nell, who runs the lake store and post office

topics.description: who Marisol thinks took the cup, and why

guests.name: Theo Calloway
guests.role: Ruth's grandson, home from engineering school, crewing for her this year
guests.voice: Nervous and sweet. All lowercase, "um", "like", trailing ellipses, apologizes a lot, 😬 and 🥹.

topics.description: where Theo was on Friday night, the night the cup disappeared

variants.text: um, the bunkhouse? all night. i didn't go anywhere, promise
bunkhouse, all night friday. like... asleep. definitely
i was in the bunkhouse all night. awake, mostly. and hal never left his bunk, like, at all. i would've noticed
bunkhouse. all night. and hal was right there in his bunk the whole time, i'm sure. pretty sure. sure

topics.description: where Theo was on Saturday night

variants.text: um, bunkhouse? same as always
bunkhouse. slept. ...mostly 😬
just the bunkhouse. nothing happened. why, did someone say something happened

topics.description: where Theo was on Sunday night, including baking late in the kitchen

variants.text: idk yet... ask me monday?
i was in the kitchen like 11:40 to 12:30. stress baking. please don't tell gran
kitchen, 11:40 til about half twelve, making bread. it helps me calm down ok

topics.description: the missing Regatta Cup and when Theo last saw it

variants.text: gran held it up at the toast like it was a baby lol. that was at ten, then it went back on the mantel
on the mantel after the ten o'clock toast. gran's gonna be so sad if we don't find it 🥹

topics.description: Theo's college plans: quitting engineering for pastry school without telling his grandmother

variants.text: ok please please don't tell gran. i quit engineering. i'm going to pastry school in the fall. i just... haven't figured out how to say it 😬
fine. yes. i dropped engineering, i got into pastry school. gran thinks i'm building bridges. i'm building croissants

topics.description: the lodge kitchen late at night: flour on the counter, the stand mixer, someone baking

variants.text: flour? um. maybe gran was baking? idk 😬
the kitchen's just... the kitchen. why is everyone asking about the kitchen

topics.description: Theo's phone and why the Wi-Fi log shows it in the kitchen on Friday night

variants.text: oh that! i left my phone charging in the kitchen friday. all night. so that's why. i was asleep
my phone was on the charger in the kitchen all night, i forgot it there. i was in the bunkhouse asleep. totally normal

topics.description: the bunkhouse Theo shares with Hal, and who comes and goes from it at night

variants.text: just me and hal out there. he snores like a boat horn lol
hal never left the bunkhouse friday. i was right there. awake. so

topics.description: next Saturday's regatta and Theo crewing on his grandmother's boat

variants.text: i'm crewing for gran this year since hal's out. i'm kind of terrified tbh
gran says i trim the jib like i'm 'folding a napkin'. i think that's bad

topics.description: what Theo and Hal were talking about in low voices in the bunkhouse late on Saturday night

variants.text: ?? nothing's happened tonight
voices? um. we were just talking about. sailing. knots. 😬
hal and me were just... chatting. about the race. normal stuff. can we talk about something else

topics.description: anything Theo noticed late on Sunday night, such as the boathouse door left open

variants.text: it's not sunday night yet lol
i didn't see anyone, i was in the kitchen 11:40 to 12:30 with the oven going

topics.description: Ruth, Theo's grandmother and the host

variants.text: gran's the best. she's gonna be so mad about the cup. and. other stuff
she taught me to sail when i was six. she's kind of my hero ngl 🥹

topics.description: Hal, Ruth's longtime crew, who shares the bunkhouse with Theo

variants.text: hal's cool, he's like my sailing uncle. he was snoring away at like quarter to one friday, i remember that
hal? he was dead asleep at 12:45 friday, snoring. i um. happened to be awake
hal? he was snoring away at 12:45 friday and he never left his bunk all night. like at all. i'm sure
he was snoring at quarter to one and he never left his bunk all night. i'd know

topics.description: Marisol, Ruth's sailing rival

variants.text: marisol scares me a little ngl. she asked gran a LOT about the new sails at dinner

topics.description: Lena, the retired doctor who goes owl-watching

topics.description: Nell, who runs the lake store and post office

variants.text: nell 😬 um. please don't ask nell about me
she's nice! she just like. reads everyone's mail. basically

topics.description: who Theo thinks took the cup, and why

variants.text: um i really don't know... marisol asked gran a LOT about the sails at dinner?? but that's probably nothing, sorry 😬
i don't want it to be anyone... maybe marisol? she really wants to win 😬

topics.description: anything Theo saw or heard during Friday night, the night of the theft: noises, lights, people up and about

variants.text: um, nothing? i was in the bunkhouse all night
nope. bunkhouse, all night, sleeping. nothing to hear 😬
i didn't take it!! ok, i was in the kitchen friday, like 12:50 to quarter to 2, baking. i heard the front door around 1:05 and hid in the pantry. that's it i swear

dictionary.goodnight: gonna go to bed, sorry, ask me tomorrow?

guests.name: Nell Haggerty
guests.role: Runs the lake's general store and post office, Ruth's neighbor
guests.voice: Gossip in full flow. "honey", "between you and me", CAPITALS for the juicy bits, long breathless messages, ☕👀.

topics.description: where Nell was on Friday night, the night the cup disappeared

variants.text: honey I was OUT by eleven, earplugs in, Ruth's guest bed is a DREAM. didn't hear a thing and I am FURIOUS about it ☕
asleep by eleven with my earplugs, which means I missed the most exciting night this lake has had in YEARS

topics.description: where Nell was on Saturday night

variants.text: tonight? bed early, honey, I open the store at six
in bed, though somebody was clomping out to the dock past midnight. Lena and her OWLS, bless her 🦉
slept, mostly! Lena went out owling on the dock after midnight and woke me right up

topics.description: where Nell was on Sunday night, including her drive to the store to check the cooler

variants.text: I've got to run to the store Sunday night, that big cooler's on the fritz again
drove to the store at nine to baby that cooler, back by ten to ten, bed by eleven. thrilling, I know ☕
nine o'clock, store, cooler, back before ten. the milk survived, thank you for asking

topics.description: the missing Regatta Cup and when Nell last saw it

variants.text: that cup's got EVERY winner since 1971 on it, honey. it was right there on the mantel after the toast at ten
saw it on the mantel after Ruth's toast at ten. and now it's GONE. I've got CHILLS 👀

topics.description: the regatta entry list Nell keeps at her store, and who paid to enter a boat this year

variants.text: between you and me 👀 Hal came in Thursday and paid the entry for his OWN boat. Second Wind! first time in twenty years he's not crewing for Ruth. and Ruth has NO idea
the entry list? honey, the big news is Hal. paid me Thursday to race Second Wind himself. first time EVER ☕

topics.description: the old lake saying about the winner keeping the cup on the mantel for luck

variants.text: "cup on the mantel, skipper on the water" and honey, people around here BELIEVE it. I could name someone who'd want that cup off Ruth's mantel before race day 👀
oh the old saying! my granddaddy swore by it. some folks still do. SOME folks very much do ☕

topics.description: the general rumors and gossip around the lake this weekend

variants.text: oh honey where do I START ☕ the Hendersons are selling, the ferry's late again, and somebody in this lodge is a THIEF
the lake is BUZZING. half of it thinks Marisol did it. the other half thinks a raccoon did it. I'm keeping an open mind 👀

topics.description: Nell's general store and post office on the lake

variants.text: best coffee on the lake, the only stamps for twenty miles, and a bait fridge I don't trust. come by!

topics.description: Nell's phone

variants.text: my phone? somewhere in my purse, honey. I find it about twice a day

topics.description: what Nell heard or noticed late on Saturday night, such as someone heading out to the dock

variants.text: nothing YET, honey, but the night is young 👀
I heard Lena tiptoe out to the dock past midnight with that owl app hooting. other than that? NOTHING, and I listened

topics.description: what Nell noticed late on Sunday night, such as the boathouse door left open

variants.text: ask me tomorrow, honey, I'll have the WHOLE story
well I was off at the store nine to ten, but after that I slept like a stone. I KNOW. the one night

topics.description: Ruth, the host and three-time regatta winner

variants.text: Ruth's a QUEEN. three cups in a row! she'll find out who did this and they'll never get another pie on this lake

topics.description: Hal, Ruth's longtime crew, and what he buys at Nell's store

variants.text: Hal buys a tin of cherry pipe tobacco off me every Thursday, regular as the tide. and THIS Thursday he paid a regatta entry for his own boat 👀
Hal? cherry tobacco, every single week. and Thursday he paid me to race Second Wind HIMSELF 👀 sneakier than he looks, between you and me ☕

topics.description: Marisol, Ruth's sailing rival, and her interest in Ruth's new sails

variants.text: Marisol came into my store LAST WEEK asking who sewed Ruth's new sails. who ASKS that? 👀
between you and me, Marisol's been snooping on Ruth's new sails. asked me who made them, cool as you like

topics.description: Theo, Ruth's grandson, and the mail he's been getting

variants.text: sweet boy. a BIG envelope came to my post office for him last month. from a PASTRY school. an engineering student! make of that what you will ☕

topics.description: Lena, the retired doctor who goes owl-watching

variants.text: Lena's a doll. out every night chasing owls. she'll outlive us all

topics.description: who Nell thinks took the cup, and why

variants.text: honey between you and me? somebody in this lodge is NOT telling the truth about race week ☕

topics.description: anything Nell saw or heard during Friday night, the night of the theft: noises, lights, people up and about

variants.text: honey I heard NOTHING, earplugs in and asleep by eleven, and I am still MAD about it ☕
asleep by eleven with my earplugs, so NOTHING, which is a tragedy for a woman like me 👀

well I never. I was asleep with my earplugs in, ask anybody
